copy_pick.why: Candidate 3 wears the dry-understatement directive best ('export controls feel personal,' 'redecorate Riyadh's skyline,' the Goldman closer) and avoids the overused 'grinds on' and the truncated driver of Candidate 2, while staying sharp and specific on a real story.

doom.driver: Nvidia is investigating Jensen Huang’s relationship with a Chinese spy.
doom.blurb: A PERSONAL MATTER AT THE CHIP COMPANY
doom.summary: The world's most strategically important chipmaker spent Sunday explaining that its CEO's affair partner was allegedly working for China's Ministry of State Security, which is one way to make export controls feel personal. Meanwhile the Iran war keeps billing seafarers in lives, Houthis redecorate Riyadh's skyline, and Trump says renewed strikes are 'highly unlikely', a phrase with a long history of being followed by strikes. On the bright side, Goldman's traders will have to write their own code again.

factors.name: AI Capability
factors.detail: Apple is leaning on Federighi to turn Siri into a true agent while Amazon recruits for a 'new-to-world' robot.

factors.name: Governance
factors.detail: Nvidia's board is investigating its own founder over an alleged Chinese intelligence operation, with chip-smuggler Megaspeed in the frame.

factors.name: Geopolitics
factors.detail: The Iran war, Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and Russia-Ukraine refinery hits keep several state conflicts running at once.

factors.name: Alignment
factors.detail: Goldman quietly pulling Claude Code from its trading floors is the closest thing to an alignment wobble today.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Mars may still be leaking volcanic gas, and nuking an asteroid apparently depends on which side you hit.

doom.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. A Santa Clara evening on the plaza of Nvidia's Endeavor building, with a blood-red and furnace-orange sky filling most of the frame. Hellish glare pours up from below the horizon and washes the whole scene in light. The pale glass facade is made of repeating triangles, and every pane blazes orange and crimson. Bruised-violet bands of cloud streak across the upper sky, and low fog from the bay glows ember-orange along the ground. The camera sits low, looking toward the glowing building. Two whole employees stand in the middle foreground as bold, solid silhouettes against the glare, shown full-length with heads, torsos and legs. One is a young woman with a ponytail and a lanyard badge, clutching a phone to her chest. The other is a slumped man in a hoodie with a laptop bag, head bowed. They stand close together and neither looks at the other. Their rim-lit edges glow orange, and their long shadows stretch toward the viewer as violet-maroon streaks across the pavement. Behind them, a giant sculptural green Nvidia-style eye emblem on the facade glows acid green, split by a jagged crimson crack of light that runs down the glass. A thin red line of light runs across the plaza and off toward the far horizon on the east side. Tall palms and a rank of empty glowing shuttle-stop lamps frame the sides. Everything is clearly visible, with saturated reds, oranges and violets and no black areas. The mood is quiet, menacing dread, as though something unseen has turned on the people who work here.

minor: The building's triangular facade has odd, warped geometry, with a slanted pyramid-like wing and a tilted right edge, but it still reads as a glass building.
The man's face is almost fully shadowed and his arms are hard to read, since one hand is in a pocket and the bag strap blends into his jacket. The silhouette is still clear.
The shuttle-stop lamps on the right are blocky and ambiguous, but they read as lamp posts.
The glowing crack and the red line on the plaza are bright and slightly confusing, but they match the intended symbolic elements.
The two figures' long violet shadows are dark, but the figures and the scene stay clearly readable.

dawn.driver: A desert stirs to life: Chile's Atacama erupts in its biggest floral display in decades. El Niño rains have transformed Chile's Atacama Desert into a spectacular sea of color, awakening a fleeting ecosystem of flowers and wildlife in one of the driest places on Earth.
dawn.blurb: CHILE'S DRIEST DESERT BURSTS INTO BLOOM
dawn.summary: Pink, purple and gold now carpet Chile's Atacama, one of the driest places on Earth, after El Niño rains woke its biggest floral display in decades and drew insects and wildlife out to feast. Off the California coast, two fishermen spotted a cruise ship pianist treading water and pulled him to safety after nine hours in the Pacific. And researchers following nearly 200,000 older adults found that a high-dose flu shot was linked to a nearly 55% lower risk of Alzheimer's.

factors.name: Science
factors.detail: UTHealth Houston researchers linked the high-dose flu vaccine to a nearly 55% lower Alzheimer's risk in adults over 65, and physicists found a quantum timing limit that could lead to electronics vastly faster than today's.

factors.name: Cooperation
factors.detail: Paris's Musée d'Orsay opened a permanent exhibition of art looted by the Nazis so experts can trace the rightful owners and their families.

factors.name: Human Spirit
factors.detail: Two fishermen spotted a cruise ship pianist 20 miles off California and rescued him after nine hours in the water.

factors.name: Environment
factors.detail: The Atacama's rare superbloom has turned bare desert into a sea of color, while scientists found that sticky 'marine snow' can carry six times more carbon into the deep ocean.

factors.name: Wild Card
factors.detail: Homes and temples across India glowed with lamps and fireworks for Diwali, and a Colorado family's giant fern named Jeff charmed the internet.

copy_pick.why: Candidate 3 is out for its bad-news hits, and between the two clean options Candidate 1 wins on specificity: its blurb names Chile, its summary opens on a vivid pink-purple-gold image instead of a recycled structure, and it closes on a striking flu-shot/Alzheimer's finding rather than a generic Diwa

dawn.dalle_prompt: Pixel art, 16-bit SNES style, no text, no antialiasing. NIGHT SCENE on the edge of Copiapó, Chile, along the Panamericana (Ruta 5), seen from across the empty two-lane road. The Atacama darkness fills the background: a star-dusted indigo sky, the faint silhouettes of rounded desert hills and the distant Andes, and a few tiny town lights on the horizon. The only light comes from artificial sources. A single sodium streetlamp throws a warm amber cone onto cracked, dusty asphalt and pale gravel. Beside the road stands a battered concrete-and-metal bus shelter. Its backlit advertising lightbox glows soft green and amber and shows a painted tourism poster of rolling hills blanketed in magenta flowers under a clean dawn sky. The poster has no lettering, and its glow spills across the gravel in a rectangle of color. The poster is the only place the bloom appears. A bundled stack of morning newspapers, tied with string, sits on the shelter's bench. The top front page shows a large photo of a pink flower field, and the stack is lit amber by the lamp. A woman in a wool poncho and knit cap stands whole beside the shelter, holding a steaming thermos. She looks up at the glowing poster, her face lit warm amber. A single magenta petal has blown onto the cracked asphalt at her feet, and a small green succulent grows from a crack at the base of the shelter. A lone pair of distant headlights glows far down the road. Warm amber and soft green palette, deep blue-black shadows lifting around the lit pools, a quiet feeling of clarity arriving.

minor: The woman in the poncho is seen in profile and is dark and simplified. Her face is barely readable, and the thermos and steam are small and ambiguous.

The lightbox poster is on the shelter's side wall, facing the woman, so it reads a little oddly as part of the structure. The poster glow also doesn't clearly spill across the gravel as a colored rectangle.
The newspaper stack on the bench looks like a golden, rubbly pile. The front-page flower photo and the string are hard to make out.
The magenta petal on the asphalt is a tiny pink blob and could be read as litter.
The succulent at the shelter base is a small green bush. The distant headlights are at the left edge and are tiny.
The lamp's light cone in the sky looks like a faint triangular haze, and the pool of light on the road is slightly inconsistent with it.
